answer: Retrospective co-activity clustering: each identity's transaction graph forms a vertex set, and pairs whose interaction timing correlates beyond chance get linked. A whisper of coordination—shared counterparties, synchronized quiet periods—raises the cluster's correlation score; a high score flags the cluster for audit. Attacker cost: maintaining plausible independence across N identities requires genuinely uncorrelated behavior, forcing N times the organic activity volume and real counterparty diversity, since any reused vertex pattern concentrates the signal and collapses the cover.
